title: Competing risks: a correct hazard ratio, a wrong cumulative incidence
question: When population adjustment transports a time-to-event outcome with a competing cause, does a correctly transported cause-specific hazard ratio give the right cumulative incidence in the target, and what repairs it?
design: Anchored transport with exponential cause-specific hazards, the target's competing hazard differing from the source's beyond the measured covariate; 16 cells crossing that difference, effect modification and overlap; MAIC, cause-specific STC and STC with the competing hazard recalibrated to the target's reported competing-event proportion. 1000 replicates per cell.
